title: Operator Notices, Surcharges and Significant Changes to a Packaged Itinerary
content:
A surcharge may be added after booking only on a product that allows it, only after the product's price-guarantee term has run out, and only where the party is notified at least the product's notice days before departure. The operator liaison office applies this note to every notice issued against one of Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products.

## Surcharges

A surcharge at or below the product's threshold share of the package price must be paid, and a surcharge above it entitles the party to cancel with nothing withheld or to accept a comparable alternative. A product with no surcharge right carries none at all, whatever happens to fuel prices or exchange rates.

## Significant changes to the itinerary

Where the operator changes the itinerary significantly before departure, the party may accept the change, take a comparable alternative or cancel with nothing withheld, and the choice is the party's alone.

A change of flight timing of less than 12 hours, a change of carrier or a change of room within the same grade is not a significant change.

## Several notices on one package

Several notices about the same package are not added together; the last notice standing before departure decides what is owed and what may be refused.

## Where the boundaries fall

| What the notice says | Judgement |
| --- | --- |
| A surcharge exactly at the product's threshold share of the package price | at the threshold, so it must be paid |
| A surcharge above the product's threshold share | above it, so the party may cancel with nothing withheld or accept a comparable alternative |
| A flight moved by 11 hours | less than 12 hours, so not a significant change |
| A flight moved by 12 hours | not less than 12 hours, so the materiality boundary is not met by this clause |
| A different carrier, or a different room of the same grade | not a significant change |
